_doc: Completed T-0481 ledger. Every frozen-manifest member received a dated repository/source-register review and targeted exact/variant-name sweep. Unlisted overrides use the documented no-corroboration default; pending is empty.
default_summary: No reliable record in the reviewed repository corpus and targeted exact/variant-name web sweep could be tied to this postal person with sufficient date/place discriminators. This is a documented no-corroboration result, not evidence that the person did not exist.

minard_ira.summary: City of St. Charles history identifies Ira Minard as a founder in 1834; historical accounts place him arriving through Chicago in 1833. Strong 1834 St. Charles geography conflicts with treating the May 1835 Chicago postal entry as proof of bodily Chicago residence.

candidates.basis: City of St. Charles history identifies Ira Minard as a founder in 1834.
conflicts: Strong 1834 St. Charles geography competes with Chicago residence.

herrick_ira.summary: DuPage Forest Preserve history places Ira Herrick settling the Herrick Lake/Wheaton area about 1833. DuPage homestead geography competes with the 1834 Chicago letter-list reading; a later Chicago directory entry is too late to resolve the seed.

candidates.basis: Ira Herrick settled the DuPage property about 1833.
conflicts: DuPage geography competes with the Chicago postal reading.

scarritt_isaac.summary: Methodist histories independently place Rev. Isaac Scarritt preaching in early Chicago and at/around Fort Dearborn; DuPage history places him among 1831 settlers. The evidence establishes Chicago contact and regional residence years before the 1834 postal seed, not a Chicago household at the seed date.

candidates.basis: Early Chicago/Fort Dearborn Methodist contact plus DuPage settlement.
conflicts: No proof of Chicago household at the 1834 postal date.

jackson_samuel.summary: Cook County history states Samuel Jackson arrived from Buffalo June 27, 1833 and served as foreman of Chicago harbor construction for some time. This independently corroborates the exact named Chicago person and occupation chronology; it does not prove a specific October 1834 household or July 1835 roof.

horr_raiph_c.summary: Aurora Township history places Ralph C. Horr at McCarty's Mill by the close of 1834 and elected justice of the peace in 1835; 'Raiph' is a plausible transcription variant. Aurora/Kane geography directly competes with bodily Chicago residence on the 1835 scene date.

candidates.basis: Ralph C. Horr at Aurora by close of 1834.
conflicts: Aurora geography conflicts with Chicago scene-date residence.

howard_joshua.summary: A contemporary-era military Joshua Howard is independently documented in the Midwest. Dearborn/Detroit history places that Joshua Howard at the Detroit Arsenal and returning to Dearborn in 1835, so it is unsafe to merge him with the Chicago postal person.

candidates.basis: Documented Joshua Howard at Detroit Arsenal/Dearborn.

ritchey_james.summary: Will County history places James Ritchey settling Homer Township in 1831 and sheltering at Fort Dearborn during the 1832 conflict. The same history says he returned to and resided in Will County, so Chicago contact in 1832 does not prove the May 1835 postal identity or Chicago residence.

candidates.basis: Will County settler with 1832 Fort Dearborn refuge.
conflicts: Returned to Will County; no 1835 Chicago residence bridge.

paddock_jane.summary: Cook County history says Samuel Mahaffay, a Palos settler of 1834, married Jane Paddock in 1835. Palos geography and absence of a direct Chicago bridge prevent asserting that this is the May 1835 postal person.

candidates.basis: Jane Paddock married in Palos in 1835.
conflicts: Palos geography; no direct Chicago bridge.

wooley_jeddiah.summary: La Salle land-sale records list Jeddiah Wooley repeatedly June 16-17, 1835; a U.S. Supreme Court record preserves an August 8, 1835 Chicago land-office receipt in his name. Land purchases and use of the Chicago land office do not establish a Chicago household or residence.

candidates.basis: Exact-name 1835 Illinois land transactions and Chicago land-office receipt.
conflicts: Transactions do not prove Chicago residence.
